 Edited By : Warda Zain Last Updated: 17 November 2026, 11:59 AM IST 4 min Share
 Follow us on EPFO has launched a WhatsApp service for PF subscribers. Send 'Hi' to its official number to check your balance, view the last five transactions and download your passbook. PF withdrawals through WhatsApp are not yet part of the confirmed service. 
 ❎ EPFO WhatsApp Service Checking a Provident Fund ( PF ) balance, tracking monthly contributions and downloading an account statement can now be done through WhatsApp. The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has launched a new service that allows subscribers to access selected account-related information through its verified WhatsApp facility.
 To advertise here, Contact Us 
 Union Labour and Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched the service on November 1, 2026, during EPFO's 74th Foundation Day celebrations in New Delhi. The initiative is aimed at making routine services easier to access without requiring members to navigate multiple digital platforms.
 The official EPFO WhatsApp number is +91 87964 41800 . Members can send a simple 'Hi' message to begin using the service.
 How to check your PF balance through WhatsApp 
 EPFO members can follow these steps to access their account information:
 Save the official EPFO WhatsApp number, +91 87964 41800, in your phone.
 Open WhatsApp and send 'Hi' to the number.
 Wait for the welcome message and select your preferred language.
 Choose the 'Check Balance' option from the available menu.
 Complete the identity verification process using the OTP sent to the mobile number registered with your UAN.
 If multiple PF accounts are linked to your UAN, select the relevant Member ID.
 Once verification is complete, your PF balance details will appear in the WhatsApp conversation.
 Members can also scan the QR code shared through EPFO's official communication to start the conversation.
 What PF details can you access on WhatsApp? 
 The new facility provides access to several routine account services. These include:
 PF balance: Check the amount available in your EPF account.
 Latest transactions: View details of the last five transactions.
 Passbook: Access and download your EPF passbook.
 PMVBRY assistance: Receive personalised guidance on requirements related to the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana.
 The passbook helps members track contributions and account transactions, including whether the employer's share is being credited.
 Can you withdraw PF money through WhatsApp? 
 EPFO is expanding its digital services, but subscribers should not assume that they can withdraw their PF savings through WhatsApp.
 The newly launched facility currently covers balance checks, recent transactions, passbook access and assistance with PMVBRY-related requirements. The official launch announcement does not include PF withdrawals as a WhatsApp service.
 Members who want to withdraw their PF money must continue to use the authorised EPFO claim process unless the organisation announces a separate facility.
 How to check whether your employer is depositing PF contributions 
 Checking the PF balance is not enough. Employees should also verify whether their employer is depositing the contributions deducted from their salaries.
 They can do this through the EPFO Member Passbook portal:
 Visit the official EPFO Member Passbook portal.
 Log in using your Universal Account Number (UAN) and password.
 Select the relevant Member ID if you have multiple PF accounts.
 Open the passbook to view the monthly contribution entries.
 Compare the employee and employer contributions recorded in the passbook with the PF deductions shown on your salary slips.
 This helps employees identify discrepancies between the amount deducted from their salaries and the contributions credited to their accounts.
 What if your company deducts PF but does not deposit it? 
 If your employer deducts PF from your salary but fails to credit the amount to your EPF account, you can raise a complaint with EPFO through its EPFiGMS grievance portal.
 The process involves:
 Visit the official EPFiGMS portal.
 Select the 'Register Grievance' option.
 Choose the PF Member category and enter your UAN.
 Complete the required verification.
 Explain the months for which contributions were deducted but not credited.
 Upload supporting documents, such as salary slips and PF passbook records.
 Submit the complaint and retain the registration number for future reference.
 Employees should keep copies of their salary slips and passbook entries as evidence when raising a complaint.
 What the new WhatsApp facility means for PF subscribers 
 EPFO's WhatsApp service is part of its broader effort to make provident fund services more accessible through digital platforms. With more than eight crore contributory members, even routine tasks such as checking balances and tracking transactions can involve a large number of service requests.
 The new facility makes these basic checks easier by bringing them to a messaging platform that many subscribers already use. It can also help employees monitor their accounts more regularly and identify missing contribution entries.
 However, the service does not replace the EPFO portal or UMANG app for every requirement. Account withdrawals, transfers and other claim-related processes remain separate from the WhatsApp facility.
 There is also an important security consideration. Members should use only EPFO's verified WhatsApp number and follow the official authentication process. They should never share their UAN password, banking credentials or OTP with an unknown contact claiming to offer PF assistance.
 For now, the main benefit is simpler access to routine account information, rather than the ability to complete every PF-related transaction through WhatsApp.
